q: 1. In king post truss there will be ..........
explain: A king post truss has a single central vertical post that connects the apex to the tie beam.

q: 2. Generally in latrines, kitchens and bathrooms the door used is from the type of
options: partly glazed and partly panelled door
explain: Flush doors are preferred for wet areas because they are easy to clean, offer no crevices for dirt or moisture, and can be easily made waterproof.

q: 3. The number of vertical posts in a queen post truss is ..........
explain: A queen post truss uses two vertical posts to support the rafters, allowing for a larger span than a king post truss.

q: 4. In a panelled door, the rails fixed in between the lock rail and top rail are called as
explain: The frieze rail is the intermediate horizontal member located specifically between the top rail and the lock rail.

q: 5. Generally the thickness of rails and styles adopted in a door frame is
explain: For standard domestic doors, a thickness of 30mm to 40mm (3-4 cm) provides the necessary structural rigidity without being excessively heavy.

q: 6. Queen-post trusses are used when the span is ..........
explain: Queen post trusses are suitable for spans ranging from 8 to 12 meters.

q: 7. In a residential building, the width of a door cannot be less than
explain: While internal doors for bathrooms can be 0.75m, the general standard for habitable rooms in a residential building is 0.9m to allow for furniture and occupant movement.

q: 8. Combination of king-post truss and queen post truss is used when the span is ..........
explain: For spans greater than 12 meters, combined trusses or steel trusses are used to provide adequate structural support.

q: 9. As compared to the floor area of a room, the glass area in a window should not be less than
explain: For adequate daylighting, building codes typically require the window glass area to be at least 1/10th (10%) of the floor area.

q: 10. A truss is called a composite truss when it ..........
options: has two slopes on each side
is a combination of king and queen post-trusses
is made of two different materials
explain: A composite truss uses two different materials, typically timber for compression members and steel/wrought iron for tension members.

q: 11. A horizontal member fixed in door or window frame for the separation of fan light is known as
explain: A transom is the horizontal structural beam that separates a door from a window above it (the fanlight).

q: 12. Steel trusses have almost replaced the timber trusses because ..........
options: they can be used for large spans
they are more economical than timber and easy to fabricate
they are fire-proof, more strong and permanent
explain: Steel trusses offer superior strength, durability, and fire resistance, and are more cost-effective for industrial or large-scale construction.

q: 13. The horizontal member forming the bottom of the frame is called as
explain: The sill is the lowest horizontal part of the window or door frame, designed to shed water away from the opening.

q: 14. When more lighting is required inside the buildings such as workshops and factories with fairly large spans ..........
explain: North-light roofs have a steep glazed side facing north to provide uniform, glare-free natural light into large floor areas.

q: 15. The window provided on the sloping roof a building is called as
explain: A dormer window is a vertical window that projects from a sloping roof, creating extra headroom and light in an attic.

q: 16. The projection of tread beyond the riser is 'called as
explain: Nosing is the rounded edge of the tread that extends over the riser to provide more foot space and improve safety.

q: 17. The extreme support of a hand railing provided at the top and bottom of a flight is known as
explain: A newel post is the heavy vertical post at the start or end of a stair flight that provides structural anchoring for the handrail.

q: 18. The head room in a staircase should not be less than
explain: The minimum vertical clearance (headroom) measured from the pitch line to the ceiling must be 2.1m to prevent tall users from hitting their heads.

q: 19. A semi-circular moulding provided on the edges of wood is known as ..........
explain: Beading is a decorative semi-circular strip or moulding used to finish edges or joints in woodwork.

q: 20. While designing a stair, the product of rise and going is approximately kept equal to
explain: One of the standard rules for comfortable stairs is (Rise in cm x Going in cm) ≈ 400 to 450. Option 420 is the most common target.

q: 21. When a member is subjected to both compression and tension, the type of lengthening joint to be used is ..........
explain: A tabled joint is a scarf joint where the two pieces are notched to interlock, making it strong in both tension and compression.

q: 22. The under surface of stair is called as
explain: The soffit refers specifically to the exposed underside of any architectural element, including stairs, arches, or cornices.

q: 23. The joint commonly used in wooden trusses where struts and ties meet ..........
explain: A bridle joint is used at the junction of rafters and tie beams or struts in timber trusses for strong, angled connections.

q: 24. The additional support given to the nosing in a wooden stair is known as
explain: Scotia is a concave molding placed under the nosing of a tread to strengthen the joint and provide a finished look.

q: 25. The tool normally used by carpenters to plane the surface ..........
explain: The jack plane is the general-purpose plane used for initial smoothing and reducing the thickness of timber.

q: 26. In a stair, the ratio of the vertical distance covered and the horizontal distance occupied by a flight is called as
explain: Gradient is the ratio of Rise to Going (Rise/Going), defining the steepness of the flight.

q: 27. The tool used for cutting small moulding along the edges ..........
explain: A rebate (or rabbet) plane is designed to cut rectangular grooves or recesses along the edges of wooden members.

q: 28. In a stair the best and most suitable position for providing winders is
explain: Providing winders at the bottom of a stair is safer and more aesthetically pleasing than placing them at the top, where they pose a greater trip hazard.

q: 29. In doors and windows, style is ..........
options: the vertical member of the frame
the vertical member of the shutter
the member which divides the frame into vertical portions
explain: Styles are the outermost vertical members of a door or window shutter.

q: 30. The width of stair in a residential building cannot be less than
explain: A minimum of 80cm to 90cm is required to allow for one person to comfortably ascend or carry items.

q: 31. When both the flights in a stair run at right angles to each other, then that stair is classified as
explain: A quarter-turn stair changes direction by 90 degrees, usually at a landing.

q: 32. The horizontal members of the frame which divides the window horizontally is ..........
explain: A transom is the horizontal member of a frame that separates a door from a window above it or divides a window horizontally.

q: 33. If landing is not to be counted then the number of treads as compared to risers in a stair are
explain: In a single flight, the last step up lands on the floor level, meaning there is always one less tread than there are risers (T = R - 1).

q: 34. A vertical member of the frame which divides the window vertically is ..........
explain: A mullion is the vertical member of a frame that divides the window into two or more separate lights or shutters.

q: 35. The dimensions of a door or window frame are measured ..........
options: outer to outer on vertical side and inner to inner on the other side
outer to outer on vertical side and outer to outer on both sides
inner to inner on both sides
explain: Door/window sizes are typically specified by the external dimensions of the frame to fit the masonry opening.

q: 36. The door designated as 10 DT 20 means ..........
options: a single shuttered door of 1 m x 2 m
a double shuttered door of 1 m x 2 m
a single shuttered door of 2 m x 1 m
a double shuttered door of 2 m x 1 m
explain: In code designation: 10 refers to width (10 dm = 1 m), DT refers to Double Shutter, and 20 refers to height (20 dm = 2 m).

q: 37. The depression on the recess made inside the door frame to receive the shutter is called ..........
explain: A rebate is the continuous step or groove cut into the frame into which the shutter fits when closed.

q: 38. The sill of window in residential buildings is generally kept above the floor level by ..........
explain: Window sill height is usually kept at 75-90 cm from the floor to align with table/desk height and provide safety.

q: 39. A door in which the shutter is formed by joining the vertical wooden boards side by side with tongue and grooved joints and which are fixed together by horizontal supports is called ..........
explain: Battened and ledged doors consist of vertical boards (battens) held together by horizontal members (ledges).

q: 40. In the battened and ledged door, the horizontal wooden boards holding the battens together are called ..........
explain: Ledges are the horizontal wooden members to which the vertical battens are secured.

q: 41. The inclined wooden boards which provide additional strength to battens in the battened and ledged door are called ..........
explain: Braces are diagonal members used between ledges to prevent the door from sagging (making it a 'Battened, Ledged, and Braced' door).

q: 42. The type of door used when good lighting is to be permitted into the room ..........
explain: Sash doors (or glazed doors) contain glass panels to allow light transmission while providing a closure.

q: 43. The type of door used when good ventilation is required in the room and at the same time privacy is maintained ..........
explain: Louvered doors have inclined slats (louvers) that allow air to pass through while blocking the line of sight for privacy.

q: 44. The type of door commonly used for garages, shops, and godowns ..........
explain: Rolling shutter doors are made of interlocking steel slats that roll up, providing high security and space efficiency for commercial use.

q: 45. The window in which the shutters can rotate either horizontally or vertically ..........
explain: Pivoted windows have shutters that swing on pivots fixed at the center (either top/bottom or sides), allowing rotation for ventilation.

q: 46. A small window fixed at a greater height than the regular window (generally 30 to 50 cm below the roof level) is called ..........
explain: Ventilators are positioned near the ceiling to allow the escape of hot, foul air and the entry of fresh air, following the principle of convection.

q: 47. A vertical window provided on the sloping roof is known as ..........
explain: A dormer window is a vertical window that projects from a sloping roof, providing light and ventilation to the attic space.

q: 48. The fixture fixed on the external doors where pad locks are to be used is known as ..........
explain: An aldrop is a common door fixture consisting of a long bolt and a slotted plate designed specifically to receive a padlock for security.

q: 49. Joining two wooden boards at an oblique angle is termed ..........
explain: Mitring involves cutting the ends of two members at an angle (usually 45°) so they form a neat corner joint, commonly used in frames.

q: 50. The usual way of specifying the screws used in wood work is by ..........
explain: Wood screws are primarily categorized and sold by their length and gauge (diameter), with length being the most common specification.
